matchstick.title: Move vertical I-stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Transfer a single vertical matchstick that forms an I from one numeral to another to adjust their numeric values while keeping both numerals valid. This is useful when the equation is off by a value of one and a simple I transfer can restore balance.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the current equality is close and moving an I between numerals could balance the values without breaking any symbol.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from an I in a numeral and leaving the source numeral without any sticks, resulting in an invalid character.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First try moving a stick within the same character to change its shape (e.g., turning X into V or I into L) before moving sticks between characters. Intra‑character changes preserve the total stick count and often yield a valid solution with minimal disruption.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of the search, before considering inter‑character moves.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the possibility of turning an X into a V and instead moving a stick from one numeral to another, missing a simpler solution.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, ensure that both the character that lost the stick and the character that gained it still correspond to a legal Roman numeral or operator. Invalid symbols invalidate the entire transformation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after each candidate move, before any arithmetic check.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from the equals sign, leaving it with a single horizontal line, which is no longer a valid "=".

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: Diagonal sticks must appear in pairs to form a V or X; a lone diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral. Ensure that any removal of a diagonal does not leave a solitary diagonal character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a diagonal stick is taken from an X or V.
matchstick.example: Taking one diagonal from an X and leaving a single diagonal stick as a standalone character.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign. The detached vertical stick can then be reused elsewhere, often to augment a numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a plus sign and a vertical stick is needed elsewhere.
matchstick.example: Removing the horizontal stick from a plus sign instead of the vertical, leaving an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new Roman numeral (e.g., a single vertical stick becomes an I). This can adjust the total value of a side when no existing character can absorb the stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a stick would otherwise leave the source or destination invalid, consider forming a new numeral from the stick.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick to a blank space that does not align with any character, creating a stray I that does not belong to the equation.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equality, explore moving a stick from one character to another, ensuring both remain valid. This expands the search space beyond single‑character modifications.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character possibilities without success.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from an X to a V without checking that the source X becomes invalid.

matchstick.title: Swap operators via horizontal stick move
matchstick.principle: Moving a horizontal stick from the equals sign to a minus (or plus) sign swaps the two operators while preserving the total stick count. This can change the arithmetic relationship between the sides.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both "=" and another operator and a simple operator swap might balance the equation.
matchstick.example: Swapping "=" and "-" but failing to verify that the resulting arithmetic equality holds.

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: After converting a plus sign to a minus by removing its vertical stick, attach that stick to a nearby numeral to increase its value (e.g., adding an I). This often restores balance after the operator change.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after a plus‑to‑minus conversion, look for a numeral that can accept the extra vertical stick without becoming invalid.
matchstick.example: Converting a plus to a minus and leaving the removed vertical stick unused, resulting in an unchanged equation.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: After forming new Roman numerals and operators, compute their numeric values to ensure the equation is mathematically true. Symbolic validity alone is insufficient.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After a candidate transformation passes symbol validation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Performing a stick move that yields syntactically correct symbols but not checking that the left‑hand side equals the right‑hand side, leading to a false equation.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to search inter‑character moves first, missing simpler intra‑character solutions.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Systematically attempt intra‑character stick relocations on each symbol before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Assuming sticks retain their orientation and not rotating horizontals to verticals (or vice versa) when repositioning
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model interprets matchsticks as fixed‑direction objects and avoids orientation changes.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that a stick can be placed in any allowed orientation for the target character, as long as the resulting symbol is valid.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on syntactic validity and overlooks the final arithmetic check.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any successful symbol transformation, always calculate the values of both sides and verify the equality before accepting the move.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., = ↔ -) automatically solve the puzzle
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overestimates the impact of operator changes and neglects arithmetic consequences.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat operator swaps as any other move: after swapping, recompute the arithmetic to ensure the equality holds.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the I↔L transformation (adding/removing a horizontal stick to/from an I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model is unaware that an I can become an L with a single horizontal addition or removal.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Include the I↔L conversion as a possible intra‑character transformation when exploring stick moves.
